beats.text: Descartes tried an experiment: doubt everything that could possibly be false.
The senses lie. Dreams feel real. Even maths, he imagined, could be a demon's trick.
He tore it all down, looking for one thing that could not be doubted away.
Then he saw it. To be deceived, to doubt at all, there must be someone doing the doubting.
"I think, therefore I am." The very act of questioning proves a questioner exists.
On that single unshakeable point, he tried to rebuild all of human knowledge.
Strip away everything you think you know, and one fact remains: you are here, thinking.

attribution: René Descartes · Discourse on the Method
source_note: Quote: Discourse on the Method, trans. John Veitch (public domain).
